dish: Nankotsu sōki soba (軟骨ソーキそば) — Yaeyama soba with soft braised pork cartilage, broth from local moromi-pork bones; also spicy miso vegetable soba
w: A Tonoshiro soba shop facing Manta Park that won the grand prix of the Yaeyama-soba division at the 3rd Yaeyama Soba Championship (2017). Tabirai describes it as a locals' favourite for its soft-cartilage sōki soba and spicy miso vegetable soba, made with a broth from island moromi-pork bones; the Okinawa Times reported FamilyMart selling a cup-noodle version supervised by the shop.

dish: Sumubari soba (すむばりそば) — Miyako soba topped with tender local island octopus; also squid-ink octopus soba
n: Oshokujidokoro Sumubari, Karimata (お食事処 すむばり)
w: A shokudō by the approach to Ikema Ōhashi that specialises in Miyako's little-known local octopus: its signature 'Sumubari soba' and an ink-black octopus soba use tako from the nearby fishing ports. Tabirai lists it among nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for; Smart Magazine explains how the kitchen makes the octopus so tender.

dish: Miyako-jima mango smoothie (宮古島マンゴースムージー) — made to order from 100% Miyako-grown mango
n: AOSORA PARLOR, Kurima Island (AOSORA パーラー)
w: A Kurima Island smoothie stand opened in 2013, with 20-plus smoothies made to order rather than batched; the signature uses 100% Miyako-grown mango. Hammocks in the garden and a gift shop alongside make it a stop on the Maehama–Kurima drive, per Tabirai and Mapple.

dish: Sazae soba (サザエそば) — Miyako soba topped with turban-shell sea snail, served only here
w: A pink-fronted seafood shokudō at the Ikema Island end of Ikema Ōhashi, looking out over 'Ikema blue'. Its turban-shell sazae soba is found nowhere else, per Tabirai's list of nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for; the Miyako island tourism association also lists its handmade purple-sweet-potato mochi.

dish: Yushi-dōfu soba (ゆし豆腐そば) — Miyako soba topped with soft, freshly curdled house island tofu
n: Shima Tōfu Haru-obaa Shokudō, Miyako (島とうふ 春おばぁ食堂)
w: A shokudō built around a family island-tofu business of more than 60 years; its most popular dish is yushi-dōfu soba, Miyako soba crowned with soft freshly-set tofu. Tabirai includes it in its nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for, and Mapple lists it among Miyako's top-ten Miyako soba lunches.

dish: Kaisen-don (海鮮丼) built on line-caught Sarahama bonito with tuna, island octopus and squid; also goma-zuke-don with umibudo
n: Ōbanmai Shokudō, Irabu Island (おーばんまい食堂)
address: 1 Maezatozoe, Irabu (Sarahama fishing port), Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan
w: The fishing co-operative's own canteen at Sarahama port on Irabu, one of Okinawa's leading pole-and-line bonito grounds; it reopened under this name in 2018. Its seafood bowls use bonito plus 3–5 fish landed that day, and Tabirai lists it among nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for for its new 'gyokyō soba'.

dish: Hawaiian-style garlic kuruma prawns (車海老ガーリックシュリンプ) — Kume-farmed kuruma-ebi; also a kuruma-prawn burger
n: YUNAMI FACTORY, Kume Island (ユナミファクトリー)
address: 1146-1 Kanegusuku, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
w: A container café that serves Kume Island's farmed kuruma prawns Hawaiian-style, to make the island's signature (and pricey) prawn an everyday food; garlic shrimp is the signature. Smart Magazine and Tabirai both feature it, Tabirai calling it the cutting edge of Kume's food scene.
